# Jubilees Chapter 30 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 30:2 — age of Dinah

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "she was a little girl, twelve years of age" | Literal; the Ge'ez specifies the age explicitly |
| LOGOS | "She was a young girl, twelve years of age" | "Young girl" slightly softens "little girl" while keeping the age |
| PNEUMA | "She was twelve years old" | Stripped of descriptive qualifier |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "young girl, twelve years of age." The age specification is significant — Jubilees makes explicit what Genesis does not, underscoring the severity of the crime. "Young girl" is preferable to "little girl" as slightly more precise.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 30:6-7 — Jacob displeased but God not displeased

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Jacob was displeased... but the LORD was not angry with them" | Literal contrast |
| LOGOS | "Jacob was displeased... But the LORD was not displeased" | Parallel structure mirrors the Ge'ez contrast |
| PNEUMA | "Jacob was furious... But God did not share Jacob's outrage" | Dynamic, explicit contrast |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS parallel structure. The Ge'ez deliberately mirrors the same root in both clauses to create the contrast (displeased/not displeased). PNEUMA's phrasing is more explicit but loses the verbal symmetry. This contrast is theologically central to the chapter.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 30:7 — "zeal for righteousness"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "acted in zeal for righteousness" | Literal; "zeal" is the operative term for Phinehas-model action |
| LOGOS | "acted with zeal for righteousness" | Same, slightly more natural |
| PNEUMA | "acted out of righteous passion" | Softens "zeal" into "passion" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "acted with zeal for righteousness." "Zeal" is the specific technical term in Second Temple literature for this category of extrajudicial protective violence (cf. Phinehas in Num 25; 1 Macc 2). PNEUMA's "passion" misses the technical register.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 30:19-20 — "heavenly tablets" formulation

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "written down as righteous in the heavenly tablets" | Literal Ge'ez formulation |
| LOGOS | "recorded as righteous in the heavenly tablets" | "Recorded" more natural for inscribed documents |
| PNEUMA | "inscribed in the heavenly tablets" | Shorter, drops "as righteous" in PNEUMA's v.19 |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "recorded as righteous in the heavenly tablets." EMET's "written down" is acceptable but "recorded" better conveys the formal documentary register. PNEUMA's shorter version loses "as righteous" which is textually present and theologically important.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 30:22 — grounding of Levitical priesthood

This verse is unique in the corpus: the priesthood is explicitly grounded in Levi's zeal at Shechem, not at Sinai (contrast Exod 32) or with Phinehas (Num 25). All three translators agreed on rendering this faithfully without smoothing the distinctive claim.

**Status:** No disagreement — the verse was translated consistently across all three.

---
